en: Taal Volcano is located on Volcano Island, which is situated within Taal Lake in the province of Batangas.
Mount Apo, located in Mindanao, is the highest mountain in the Philippines, standing at 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching over 500 kilometers through the Cagayan Valley.
The Philippine eagle is a critically endangered bird of prey endemic to the remaining tropical forests of Mindanao.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park features an eight-kilometer navigable underground river that flows directly into the sea.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 cone-shaped limestone hills that turn brown during the dry season.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park is a protected marine sanctuary in the Sulu Sea known for its high coral biodiversity.
Lake Lanao in Mindanao is the second-largest lake in the Philippines, covering an area of approximately 340 square kilometers.
Palawan is the largest province in the Philippines by land area and contains the Calamian Islands in its northern part.
Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for its nearly perfect symmetrical cone shape formed by repeated stratovolcano eruptions.
The Philippine tarsier, found in Bohol, is one of the smallest primates and has enormous eyes adapted for night vision.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao are ancient agricultural landscapes carved into the mountains by the Ifugao people over 2,000 years ago.
